5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 4

Comparatives

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Compare two people, animals or things (comparar dos cosas)
  • Form comparatives with -er and more
  • Learn the irregular comparatives better and worse
  • Use than, as… as and not as… as

Para pensar

Una jirafa mide unos 5 metros y un elefante, unos 3. ¿Cómo dirías en inglés que la jirafa es más alta?

Explicación

What is a comparative?

A comparative is the form of an adjective we use to compare two people, animals or things. «My brother is older than me.» «A plane is faster than a train.» «Maths is more difficult than Art for me.»

The word than introduces the second thing: «A than B». En castellano: «más alto que», «más rápido que». En inglés, con los adjetivos cortos no decimos «more tall», sino que el adjetivo cambia: taller. Así que hay que fijarse en el número de sílabas.

Short adjectives: -er

With short adjectives (one syllable) we add -er: tall → taller, small → smaller, fast → faster, old → older, long → longer, cold → colder, short → shorter, strong → stronger.

«Antarctica is colder than Spain.» «The Nile is longer than the Ebro.» «My grandfather is older than my grandmother.» The adjective doesn't change for plural: «These boxes are smaller than those boxes».

Spelling changes

Some short adjectives change a little. 1. Ending in -e: add only -r: nice → nicer, large → larger, safe → safer. 2. Consonant + vowel + consonant: double the last letter: big → bigger, hot → hotter, thin → thinner, fat → fatter, sad → sadder.

3. Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y: change y to -ier: happy → happier, funny → funnier, easy → easier, heavy → heavier, busy → busier. «Today is hotter than yesterday.» «This joke is funnier than yours!»

Long adjectives: more

With long adjectives (two syllables or more, not ending in -y) we put more in front: beautiful → more beautiful, expensive → more expensive, interesting → more interesting, dangerous → more dangerous, important → more important, famous → more famous.

«A shark is more dangerous than a dolphin.» «This book is more interesting than the film.» Ojo: nunca juntes las dos formas: «more taller» o «more easier» están mal. O -er, o more.

Irregular: better, worse, further

A few adjectives are irregular. You must learn them: good → better (mejor), bad → worse (peor) and far → further or farther (más lejos).

«My handwriting is better than last year.» «The weather today is worse than yesterday.» «Madrid is further from the sea than Valencia.» Truco: nunca digas «gooder» ni «more good». Piensa en el castellano: tampoco decimos «más bueno que» cuando queremos decir «mejor».

As… as and not as… as

When two things are the same, we use as + adjective + as: «Lucía is as tall as Marta» (Lucía y Marta miden lo mismo). «This bag is as heavy as that one.»

For the opposite we use not as… as: «My bike isn't as fast as yours» (mi bici es menos rápida). This is a polite way to compare. The adjective doesn't change here: we never say «as taller as».

Comparing with numbers

We can use comparatives with real data. Look at this information about animals: a cheetah runs at 110 km/h and a horse at 70 km/h. → «A cheetah is faster than a horse.» A blue whale weighs 150,000 kg and an elephant 6,000 kg. → «A blue whale is heavier than an elephant.»

We can also say how much: «A cheetah is much faster than a horse» (mucho más) or «Leo is a bit taller than Eva» (un poco más). These little words make your comparisons more precise.

Reading: city or village?

Read Irene's text: «I live in Madrid, but my grandparents live in a small village in Soria. Madrid is bigger and noisier than the village. There are more shops and the buses are faster. But the village is quieter and the air is cleaner. The winters there are colder than in Madrid, and the stars at night are brighter. The village isn't as exciting as the city, but for me it's more relaxing. In summer, I think the village is better!»

Find six comparatives with -er and two with more. Which one is irregular?

Let's practise: compare and guess

Play «Who is it?» in pairs. Think of two classmates, two animals or two famous places, and give clues: «It is bigger than a cat, but smaller than a horse. It is more friendly than a wolf.» (Answer: a dog!)

Then write five sentences comparing your town with another town, or yourself last year and now: «Now I am taller. My English is better. My homework is more difficult.» Repaso: corto → -er; largo → more; irregulares better, worse; y siempre than.

Comparatives

Ejercicios

  1. Write the comparative: small, hot, funny, nice.

  2. Write the comparative: famous, dangerous, good, bad.

  3. Complete: «A car is ___ (fast) than a bike.»

  4. Complete: «Science is ___ (interesting) than TV.»

  5. Complete: «Today the weather is ___ (bad) than yesterday.»

  6. Correct: «My house is more big that yours.»

  7. Same height: Pol 1.40 m, Gal 1.40 m. Write a sentence.

  8. Write with not as… as: «Tennis is more popular than golf.»

  9. Translate: «El Teide es más alto que el Mulhacén.»

  10. Compare yourself now and when you were five (three sentences).

Practica

  1. The comparative of «tall» is…

    1. A) more tall
    2. B) tallest
    3. C) taller

  2. The comparative of «big» is…

    1. A) bigger
    2. B) biger
    3. C) more big

  3. The comparative of «happy» is…

    1. A) happyer
    2. B) happier
    3. C) more happy

  4. The comparative of «beautiful» is…

    1. A) beautifuller
    2. B) more beautiful
    3. C) most beautiful

  5. The comparative of «good» is…

    1. A) gooder
    2. B) more good
    3. C) better

  6. «A plane is faster ___ a car.»

    1. A) than
    2. B) that
    3. C) as

  7. «This test is ___ than the last one.» (bad)

    1. A) badder
    2. B) more bad
    3. C) worse

  8. «Ana is ___ Laia.» (misma edad)

    1. A) older as
    2. B) as old as
    3. C) as older as

  9. The comparative of «nice» is…

    1. A) nicer
    2. B) niceer
    3. C) more nice

  10. Which sentence is correct?

    1. A) My bag is heavier than yours.
    2. B) My bag is more heavier than yours.
    3. C) My bag is heavyer than yours.

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el comparativo; Cuándo se añade -er y cuándo se usa more; Qué comparativos son irregulares; Cómo se dice que dos cosas son iguales con as… as.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

ComparativeCompara dos cosas: taller than.
than«que» en las comparaciones.
-erAdjetivos cortos: fast → faster.
-ierAcabados en -y: easy → easier.
moreAdjetivos largos: more expensive.
better / worseMejor / peor.
as… asIgual de: as tall as.
not as… asMenos: not as fast as.

Soluciones

  1. C) Corto: + -er.
  2. A) CVC: doble g.
  3. B) -y → -ier.
  4. B) Largo: more.
  5. C) Irregular.
  6. A) Than = que.
  7. C) Irregular.
  8. B) as + adjetivo + as.
  9. A) Acaba en -e: + r.
  10. A) heavy → heavier, sin more.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. smaller, hotter, funnier, nicer.
  2. more famous, more dangerous, better, worse.
  3. faster.
  4. more interesting.
  5. worse.
  6. My house is bigger than yours.
  7. Pol is as tall as Gal.
  8. Golf isn't as popular as tennis.
  9. El Teide is higher (taller) than Mulhacén.
  10. Model answer: Now I am taller. I am stronger. My drawings are better.
